text:
Evan (Eng - Vancouver): hey team — planning a move from Vancouver to Zurich in September. main concerns: will my monthly WFH stipend continue, payroll entity switch timing, and whether Redwood needs any Swiss VAT/corporate registration for having an employee there. also curious about health insurance start dates.
Maya (People Ops): congrats! :tada: high-level: payroll will switch to CH when you're tax resident. WFH stipend continuation depends on CH policy coverage; equipment reimbursements can be taxable differently in CH. when's your intended move date?
Evan (Eng - Vancouver): aiming for 2026-09-10 arrival, last day in Canada payroll 2026-09-05.
Olivier (Finance): note: Switzerland requires employer registration for payroll and social contributions for resident employees. that's separate from corporate tax/VAT nexus, which depends on local sales/contracting. for a single remote employee employer registration is expected.
Helena (Payroll Switzerland): workflow: 1) submit relocation form 2) Payroll issues final CA payslip and opens CH onboarding 3) obtain AHV number (Swiss social security) after registration 4) first CH pay will follow local payroll cycle after cutover. please upload bank info and ID.
Evan (Eng - Vancouver): my partner and I already bought an office chair with my stipend money — receipt processed in Canada last month. will that be fine?
Maya (People Ops): if expense was processed on Canadian payroll before cutover, we keep it. recurring stipend: if policy covers Switzerland we'll switch the monthly allowance to CH payroll; otherwise we may discontinue it. we can discuss a one-time bridging payment if there's a gap.
IntlTax: Swiss tax flags: employer registration and social contributions are required. corporate tax nexus is unlikely from a single remote engineer doing internal work, but if you sign local contracts or have recurring Swiss customers it changes. VAT registration generally tied to sales presence, not an employee alone. we'll escalate to external counsel if needed.
Olivier (Finance): also flag: equity and stock exercise taxation can be sensitive around residency change. if you have upcoming option exercises, tell us dates — withholding could differ.
Evan (Eng - Vancouver): i have an RSU vesting on 2026-10-01. should i be worried?
Helena (Payroll Switzerland): please note vesting after cutover will be subject to Swiss payroll/withholding rules; Finance will advise. add vest date to your relocation case.
Evan (Eng - Vancouver): what about health insurance? Canada coverage ends when i deregister; is there a waiting period for Swiss coverage?
Maya (People Ops): CH mandatory health insurance (KVG) must be taken out by residents typically within three months of arrival, but employer often helps with enrollment guidance. we'll include a benefits pack and a local broker contact.
Evan (Eng - Vancouver): shipping household goods — covered?
Maya (People Ops): relocation policy covers shipping up to threshold; above that we use our vendor. attach quotes to the case.
Evan (Eng - Vancouver): final practical: will September stipend be pro-rated?
Helena (Payroll Switzerland): stipend pro-ration rule: month is paid by whichever payroll entity is active on each calendar day. with a 2026-09-05 cutover, September will likely be split pro-rata CA/CH. if cutover is on the 1st we pay full from CH.
PeopleOpsBot: "Case #R-6011 created and assigned to Maya. Reminder: international payroll cutover SLA 10 business days"
Olivier (Finance): next steps: Evan, please confirm you won't sign local contracts and add RSU vesting date. we'll run a quick nexus checklist and loop in external tax counsel if anything looks off.
Evan (Eng - Vancouver): confirmed no client contracts, RSU date added. thanks team!
Maya (People Ops): i'll post a short checklist in this thread and ping 3 business days before cutover.
PeopleOpsBot: "Reminder: upload Swiss AHV and bank details within 21 days of arrival to avoid payroll fallback."
